subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI external-editor compose flow now, and what trigger plus local editor/temp-file safety contract should it use?
rationale: The implementation boundary is clear, but launching a user-selected local process and writing prompt drafts needs maintainer-approved UX and security rules before automation should implement it.

options.title: Approve guarded core flow
options.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

options.title: Hold for UX choice
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers choose the shortcut or slash-command model and resolve the inactive keybinding mismatch.

options.title: Decline process handoff
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers prefer inline multiline editing, composer expansion, or another non-process workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core flow
recommendation.body: Implement the handoff in core TUI with an approved key or slash trigger, argv-safe editor handling, restrictive temp files, cleanup, no auto-submit, status errors, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue in detail and is the strongest routing signal for the TUI product/security tradeoff.
